feed.title: TRELA
feed.subtitle: TRELA, led by Prof. Yiorgos Makris, builds trusted and reliable integrated circuits and systems by combining machine learning, statistical analysis, and hardware design, with work spanning hardware security, AI for test, analog/RF ICs, and bio-security primitives.

entry.title: TRELA is now at UC San Diego

link.title: TRELA is now at UC San Diego

entry.content:
The Trusted and RELiable Architectures (TRELA) Lab has a new home at UC San Diego. We continue our work on trusted and reliable integrated circuits and systems, from hardware security and machine learning-based test to analog/RF ICs and bio-security primitives.

Interested in joining? See the Join us page.
entry.summary: The Trusted and RELiable Architectures (TRELA) Lab has a new home at UC San Diego. We continue our work on trusted and reliable integrated circuits and systems, from hardware security and machine learning-based test to analog/RF ICs and bio-security primitives.

entry.title: New SRC project on generative AI-based test generation

link.title: New SRC project on generative AI-based test generation

entry.content: The Semiconductor Research Corporation (SRC) is funding our project “Generative AI-based Test Generation for Mixed-Signal Integrated Circuits” (2025 to 2028), which explores how large language models can learn to generate tests for integrated circuits.

entry.title: Genetic Physical Unclonable Functions in Science Advances

link.title: Genetic Physical Unclonable Functions in Science Advances

entry.content: Our manuscript “Genetic Physical Unclonable Functions in Human Cells” appears in Science Advances. The work brings the idea of hardware PUFs to living cells, enabling provenance attestation of human cell lines.
